newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee mulls privatizing all state prisons.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee mulls privatizing all state prisons.

text.p: Tennessee legislative leaders are considering turning over management of all the state's adult prisons to private companies, the leader of a key House committee said.
The move would save $100 million out of an annnual corrections budget of $450 million, according to House Finance Committee Chairman Rep. Matt Kisber, D-Jacksonville.

Kisber told reporters late Wednesday the proposal is still preliminary and has not been introduced in bill form. He said lawmakers would not proceed unless they were convinced that savings would be sufficiant, that no state prison employees would be fired and that safety would not be jeopardized.
Although several states contract with private prison companies to operate some prisons, no state has privatized its entire system.
Tennessee operates 21 adult prisons that house 13,800 inmates and employ 4,900 people. One prison is privately managed by Corrections Corporation of America, based in Nashville.
Kisber said lawmakers asked budget analysts to calculate the potential savings or prison privatization as an alternative to budget cuts proposed by Gov. Don Sundquist.
The governor's budget would cut $40 million from higher education, eliminate 1,7000 state jobs and use $88 million of Tennessee Housing Development Agency reserves for other programs.
